extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural researchers, grant applicants, program officers, and the biomedical research community
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and analysis on evaluating grant productivity, interpreting peer review percentile scores, assessing large-scale funding programs, and implementing training/funding policies for NIH/NIGMS grants. Includes recommended metrics, analysis methods, and policy considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Productivity metrics (aggregate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multiple bibliometric measures to evaluate grant productivity, including numbers of publications, citations, and highly cited citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author analyzes grants by linking funded awards to publications (and their citations) and notes that 'the numbers of publications and citations represent the simplest available metrics of productivity.' Use a suite of metrics rather than a single number because metrics are imperfect and correlated; expect substantial variability across grants and fields. The analysis used medians, interquartile ranges, and correlation coefficients between metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of publications associated with a grant (median and distribution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a basic productivity metric (e.g., median number of publications per grant was 7 with IQR 4–11). Use distributions (histograms) to show variability and consider field/publishing-style differences when interpreting raw counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Total citations to publications resulting from a grant (median and distribution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a simple productivity measure (median citations per grant reported as 73 with IQR 26–156). Consider excluding self-citations in refined analyses and correct for time dependence of citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highly cited publications (top 10% time-corrected)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of publications in the top 10% of time-corrected citations for the relevant set of research publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author defines highly cited publications as those in the top 10% of time-corrected citations and analyzes their distribution across percentile scores; notes that distribution of highly cited publications can be relatively even across percentile ranges, so interpret carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research vs. review publications distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate research articles from review articles when counting publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refined metrics should focus on research (not review) publications because they more directly reflect primary scientific output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-self citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Count citations excluding self-citations to better reflect external impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a refinement to raw citation counts, exclude self-citations to reduce inflation of impact measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-corrected citation counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust citation counts to account for the time-dependence of citations (more recent papers have had less time to accumulate citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use time-corrected citations when comparing across periods; the author used such corrections when defining 'highly cited' and when comparing publications across fiscal years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review percentile score as a predictor
rubrics_metrics.description: Use application percentile scores from peer review to predict subsequent productivity trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The analysis showed that 'peer review scores do predict trends in productivity in a manner that is statistically different from random ordering,' but also emphasizes substantial grant-to-grant variation within narrow percentile ranges. Percentile scores correlate negatively with productivity metrics (better percentiles → higher productivity), but they are not perfectly predictive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualization via running averages
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate running averages over sets of grants (e.g., sets of 100) to visualize trends in productivity metrics versus average percentile score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used separately for Type 1 (new) and Type 2 (competing renewal) grants to reveal different behaviors (Type 1 curves relatively flat; Type 2 steeper). Running averages help reveal trends amid high variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lorenz curve and Gini coefficient for concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Lorenz curves and Gini coefficients to measure how concentrated productivity metrics (like citations) are across grants ordered by percentile score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plot cumulative fraction of a metric versus cumulative fraction of grants ordered by percentile; compute Gini coefficient (twice shaded area) to quantify non-uniform distributions. Compare observed Gini to simulations/random distributions to assess statistical significance (e.g., citations Gini = 0.096, 3.5 SDs above random).

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveats in interpretation of metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize limitations when interpreting productivity metrics: metrics are imperfect, single-year data limitations, field differences, publishing styles, and legitimate sources of variability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author warns to be 'appropriately cautious' given imperfections in metrics, that the analysis reflects only a single year, and that variability arises from differences between fields and publishing styles. Avoid overinterpreting point estimates and consider broader context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment design for large-scale programs (process + outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate large-scale funding programs using both process evaluations and outcomes assessments conducted by independent, well-qualified groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIGMS engaged independent groups to articulate strengths, accomplishments, weaknesses, and challenges. Process evaluations help understand implementation; outcomes assessments judge impact. Timing of assessments matters—too early may miss impacts; too late may miss management-relevant feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect diversity among large grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that large-scale collaborative awards will differ substantially based on scientific challenge, community, and leadership approach, and that diversity can reflect a core principle rather than a flaw.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While some evaluators may see heterogeneity across awards as problematic, NIGMS argues that diversity reflects the scientific community defining problems and approaches; evaluators should account for context-specific differences rather than force uniform criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing – policy versus uptake
rubrics_metrics.description: Require and invest in rapid and open data sharing policies, but evaluate whether shared data are provided in forms the community will use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All glue grants included investments in IT and open data policies, but making data available is not equivalent to successful sharing; effective data and knowledge sharing requires attention to formats, tools, and community adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing considerations for program assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance early assessment (to inform management) with recognizing that scientific impact may take long to unfold; consider re-assessing program impact over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author notes trade-off between early evaluation for program management and the long time required for scientific advances to demonstrate impact; recommends potentially revisiting assessments later to gauge long-term outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation on structure of large-scale awards
rubrics_metrics.description: When restructuring large collaborative programs, consider smaller awards but increase number of awards to better support innovative, interdisciplinary, large-scale research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes assessment recommended discontinuing the current glue grant program and creating 'a suite of modified program(s)' with awards 'considerably smaller, but larger in number.' Use assessments' recommendations to redesign funding mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for new ideas and new investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain support for new investigators and new ideas because productivity/impact (e.g., highly cited publications) can extend across percentile ranges and new grants can show comparable high-impact output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observations that new (Type 1) grants are comparable to competing renewals for highly cited publications above certain percentiles reinforce need to continue supporting novel ideas and new investigators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage training plans in research grant applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Strongly encourage inclusion of training plans in R01 and other research grant applications that request support for graduate students or postdoctoral trainees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NIGMS Strategic Plan for Biomedical and Behavioral Research Training endorses the use of individual development plans (IDPs) for trainees and emphasizes mentoring. Training is considered broadly (not only on formal training grants), and applicants should describe training components when they request trainee support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Endorsement of individual development plans and mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote use of individual development plans for trainees and emphasize the overall importance of mentoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The strategic plan 'endorses the use of individual development plans for these trainees as well as the overall importance of mentoring,' and recognizes diverse career outcomes for trainees as contributing to the NIH mission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal policy for award adjustments under constrained appropriations
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific funding adjustments in response to appropriation changes: modular and nonmodular award adjustments, and expectations for number of new/competing awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the Full-Year Continuing Appropriations Act of 2011 (approx. 1% lower than FY2010): modular noncompeting awards awarded 1% lower than prior committed level; nonmodular grants receive no inflationary increase and are reduced by an additional 1%; previously issued awards adjusted upward to be consistent; NIGMS expected to make ~866 new and competing research project grants. Use such fiscal-management policies to balance funding across competing and noncompeting needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent two-way communication with scientific community
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide clear information and data to the research community and enable two-way dialogue so stakeholders understand NIH policies and opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Feedback Loop' was intended to promote two-way communication, reduce rumor-driven information voids, and provide data and rationales behind policies so the community can take maximal advantage of NIH opportunities. Encourage outreach, participation, and engagement.
